newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba unveils pocket phone and Internet in one.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba unveils pocket phone and Internet in one.

text.p: Toshiba Corp on Thursday unveiled a pocket-size unit that is both a telephone and notebook computer, allowing users fast access to the Internet, electronic mail and cellular phone networks.
The personal digital assistant (PDA) is the fourth of its kind to take advantage of a high-powered network launched by Japan's personal handy phone (PHS) operators on April 1.
PHS is a technology halfway between cellular and cordless phones. It costs less than full-powered cell phones and has more range than a regular cordless phone.
Kyocera Corp, Sanyo Electric Co and Matsushita Electric Industrial Co plan to start selling similar PHS-based PDAs from April.
But a Toshiba official said the Genio was the first product that combined functions of e-mail, Internet access, the PHS and personal information management.
It has a 14-cm (3.5-inch) liquid crystal display and weighs 220 grams (seven ounces), making it the world's smallest and lightest Internet viewer, a Toshiba official told a news conference.
The product is capable of storing one megabyte of data, more than any of the three rival products, the official said.
A further two megabytes of memory can be added in the form of a removable SmartMedia memory card the size of a postage stamp.
Genio will be sold in Japan from April 25, with a pricetag ranging from 50,000 yen ($415) to 70,000 yen ($585), about the same as rival products. ($=120 yen)
